completedWork: TR-D-9: src/ai/cli.js tracks every started child (per-adapter registry plus a module-level set). The adapter now exposes close() and liveChildren(). close() marks the adapter closed, sends SIGTERM to each child's process group, SIGKILLs after killGraceMs (new option, default 1000 ms, CLI_KILL_GRACE_MS), sweeps the group once the leader exits, rejects the in-flight calls with PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE, removes their temp cwd and resolves when all runs have settled; it is idempotent and later calls reject PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE without spawning (a close() that lands while the temp cwd is being made also stops the spawn). A single process 'exit' hook SIGKILLs the groups still registered, which covers process.exit() in main.js stop(). The timeout, abort and cap paths still SIGKILL the group immediately, as before. TR-D-10: test/live/run-live-model.js parses the ceiling with parseCeilingMicroUsd: the regex ^(0|[1-9][0-9]{0,11})(?:\.([0-9]{1,2}))?$ on the raw string (no trim, no sign, no exponent, no leading zero), compared in integer cents, 1..500, before any conversion; toMicroUsd is no longer used for the ceiling. The runner prints a 'cli: claude <version>' line after the plan lines and before the first call, installs SIGINT/SIGTERM handlers once the provider exists (close the adapter, say 'interrupted', no report, exit 130/143 through an injectable exit), and closes the adapter in a finally on every return path. Test fixtures: stub-claude.mjs gains child.pid in hang mode and a stubborn mode (ignores SIGTERM); cli-orphan-driver.mjs is the process.exit() driver. FINDING -> CHANGE -> TEST -> EVIDENCE. TR-D-9 / SEC-D-2 -> src/ai/cli.js registry, close(), exit hook; runner closes the adapter on SIGINT/SIGTERM and on every return path -> cli.test.js 'close() and the exit hook leave no CLI child behind' (6 tests: group kill, SIGTERM-ignoring child, closed adapter, other adapter untouched, process.exit() driver, registry empty after calls) and live-runner-refusal.test.js 'SIGINT and SIGTERM close the adapter' (in-process) plus 'the runner process kills its CLI child on SIGINT and SIGTERM' (real runner process, stub claude, exit 143 / 130, pids dead, no report); all red before the change (6 red in cli.test.js: close is not a function and three stub children were left running; 3 red in the refusal file) -> ev:ev-mv34amer-0143b344 (plan command, 107/107, ECCODE_EVAL 200/200 fake) and ev:ev-mv34bp0u-01821bb8 (npm test). TR-D-10 -> parseCeilingMicroUsd, badCeiling message, CLI version line before the first call -> live-runner-refusal.test.js 'NFR3: the ceiling is a decimal with at most two fraction digits, from 0.01 to 5.00, checked BEFORE any rounding (TR-D-10)': 38 refused values in evaluateLaunch, 6 through the real process (exit 2, empty stdout, fixed message), 5, 5.00 and 0.50 accepted through --dry-run; red before the change -> same two evidence ids.
remainingIssues: Decision: '05' and '005.00' are refused (a leading zero is non-canonical for a spend limit); '5.0' and '0.5' are accepted (one fraction digit is within 'at most two'). close() is idempotent and terminal. The timeout, abort and 8 MiB cap paths keep the immediate process-group SIGKILL (existing guarantee); SIGTERM then SIGKILL applies to close().

A parent killed by SIGKILL (or by SIGTERM with no handler) cannot run any hook, so its CLI child is still orphaned in that case; the child is bounded by --max-budget-usd and the reservation sweep settles it. The server and the live runner both handle SIGTERM/SIGINT and close the adapter, so only an uncatchable kill leaves a child. The exit hook runs on process.exit() and on a normal end.
